target_customer: Online merchants and businesses in Pakistan that need to accept card and local payments
problem: Pakistani businesses had no simple developer friendly way to accept international and local online payments.
business_model: Payment processing fees on a regulated payment gateway and orchestration platform
product_category: Payment gateway and developer payments API

founders.name: Ziyad Parekh
education: Double major in Mathematics and Economics (institution not named)
founders.background_notes: From the YC page; a Medium fireside chat says he began it as a side project and launched in May 2019.

founders.name: Raza Naqvi
founders.background_notes: Named as co-founder in ProPakistani February 2021 coverage and the Ejad Labs fireside chat; not listed on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Payment gateway integration with banks, card processors and local rails requires compliance and reliability work, with a regulatory licence on top.

defensibility.rationale: SBP licences are scarce; ProPakistani says Safepay was the first to get a commercial licence in five years (April 2025), and merchants integrate deeply.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition found; Safepay partnered with UBL, Euronet and Visa Cybersource instead.

market_need_then: Pakistan lacked a Stripe like gateway; Safepay launched in May 2019 and pitched itself at Demo Day as the Stripe of Pakistan, serving over 300 merchants by early 2021 per coverage.

branding.domain_note: Uses getsafepay.pk with a get prefix.

brand_strength.rationale: Descriptive name shared with other payment products; press framed it by the Stripe comparison rather than the brand.

pivots.from: Peer to peer payments platform modeled on Venmo (one source says it began in 2017)
pivots.why: Single source, not opened; treat as unconfirmed

outcome_analysis: Safepay was the first Pakistani fintech through YC, raised a seven figure seed led by Stripe in February 2021, and won SBP pilot approval in August 2022 and a commercial licence in April 2025. The licence position is a real moat in a thin market, though outside funding amounts are small or undisclosed.
notes: Seed round stated by ProPakistani, Geo and Dawn as seven figures with no amount, so amount is null. A standout.work profile lists 5.5M total and Series A, unverified and not recorded. YC gave 150K per ProPakistani; not recorded as a round. Dawn August 2022 mentions another recently closed round, no details found. Competitors: PayPro appears only in undated pages, none dated near 2020, so the list is empty. Prior employers not found.
